title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the setup from the previous page. There, E is a module on S (over T) with a connection d^0_E : E → E⊗Ω^1_{S/T}. The connection extends uniquely to a degree-1 operator d^•_E on E⊗Ω^•_{S/T} satisfying the graded Leibniz rule. The connection is integrable when the curvature d^1_E∘d^0_E vanishes, which is exactly when (E⊗Ω^•_{S/T}, d^•_E) is a complex. This page then sets up the standard machinery of algebraic de Rham cohomology with coefficients.

(11) defines H^*_DR(S,E) as the hypercohomology ℍ^*(S, E⊗Ω^•_{S/T}). The connection δ_E (equivalently d^0_E) is understood as part of the data of E.

(12) gives the 'Hodge-to-de Rham' (first hypercohomology) spectral sequence E_1^{pq} = H^q(S, E⊗Ω^p_{S/T}) ⇒ H^{p+q}_DR(S,E). It comes from the trivial ('stupid', bête) filtration of the complex.

(13) gives the edge map H^*(Γ(S, E⊗Ω^•)) → H^*_DR(S,E). This is an isomorphism when S is affine, since the terms are quasi-coherent.

(14)/(15) give maps H^i_DR(S,E) → H^i(S,E). These are induced by the morphism of complexes E⊗Ω^•_{S/T} → E (= E in degree 0). This is the quotient by σ_{≥1}, which Grothendieck calls 'troncation'.

NB: as E varies over modules with integrable connection, H^*_DR is a δ-functor (better: defined at the level of derived categories), and all the maps above are functorial in E.

Re NB: for a commutative square S'→S over T'→T, inverse images of connections are defined and 'everything follows'. In particular:
(a) base change along T'→T, with S' = S×_T T';
(b) for S→T'→T, a connection relative to T induces one relative to T'. This is the first ingredient toward the Gauss–Manin setup.

The next page studies (14) for i = 0, 1. For i = 0 one gets horizontal sections. For i = 1, H^1 of a complex is described via K^0-torsors with a trivialisation of the induced K^1-torsor. Purpose: preliminaries for the Gauss–Manin connection and the Cartier operator / p-curvature.
errors: Not an error but implicit: the isomorphism (13) for S affine needs E (and Ω^p_{S/T}) quasi-coherent; the page does not state this.

The map (14) is to the cohomology of E as a sheaf of abelian groups (f^{-1}O_T-modules). Calling (15) 'troncature' refers to the stupid truncation σ_{≤0}, not the canonical truncation. Both are minor; no mathematical error.

ideas.what: Integrable connection ⇔ E⊗Ω^• is a complex; de Rham cohomology with coefficients as hypercohomology
ideas.modern_name: algebraic de Rham cohomology of a flat connection

ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (Publ. IHES 29, 1966); 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968)

Base change and restriction of connections under commutative squares S'→S, T'→T

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard expository preliminaries: de Rham cohomology with coefficients, the Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence, and functoriality. All are well documented (Katz–Oda, Katz 1970, Deligne's 'Équations différentielles'). The only mildly interesting remark is the insistence on a derived-category formulation, which is also standard.
